impact_scope.description: JPEG SOS decoding now detects a closed input stream, appends internal zero padding once when space permits, and stops requesting more input. H0 already supplies the fuzz input through src and reaches SOS decoding through the existing decode_image_config/decode_frame flow.
A new internal bitstream_is_closed flag prevents repeated padding and is cleared by the already-existing restart_frame operation.

evidence: In S0, H0 initializes the JPEG decoder and drives the supplied src through decode_image_config, decode_frame_config, and decode_frame, exposing JPEG entropy input through the established image-decoder API.
S0 already had the public restart_frame entry, while H0 did not call it; the commit scope introduces no pre-existing caller-controlled closed-bitstream mode that H0 failed to select.

In S1, the new args.src.is_closed() behavior is reached through the same decode_frame call and caller-supplied src already used by H0; no additional entry, argument, configuration, or input format is required.

bitstream_is_closed and its reset in restart_frame are internal decoder state. The existing restart_frame API and its caller-facing call sequence and arguments are unchanged, so H0's omission of that entry is not newly worsened.

new_harness_obligation.description: The commit adds no new public call, caller-supplied argument or buffer, call-order transition, configuration action, compile-time enablement, or input construction. Closed-input handling occurs automatically within the existing JPEG decode path, and restart_frame only gains an internal-state reset.
evidence: decode_sos still receives the existing src and workbuf parameters.
H0 already passes src into the decoder's standard decode operations.
restart_frame retains the same index and io_position arguments and the same externally visible call-sequence checks.

reason: The fuzz-relevant change is automatic handling of a closed JPEG entropy stream plus bookkeeping for that handling. H0 already exposes caller-supplied JPEG bytes through the affected decode path. The added flag and reset do not create caller control requirements, and the existing restart_frame entry is neither new nor changed in its external protocol. Therefore there is no material same-scope gap on either side and no new harness obligation.
